statement: If from a straight line there be subtracted a straight line which is incommensurable in square with the whole and which with the whole makes the sum of the squares on them medial, twice the rectangle contained by them medial, and further the squares on them incommensurable with twice the rectangle contained by them, the remainder is irrational; and let it be called that which produces with a medial area a medial whole.
heath_proof: For from the straight line AB let there be subtracted the straight line BC incommensurable in square with AB and fulfilling the given conditions; [X. 35] I say that the remainder AC is the irrational straight line called that which produces with a medial area a medial whole. For let a rational straight line DI be set out, to DI let there be applied DE equal to the squares on AB, BC, producing DG as breadth, and let DH equal to twice the rectangle AB, BC be subtracted. Therefore the remainder FE is equal to the square on AC, [II. 7] so that AC is the “side” of FE. Now, since the sum of the squares on AB, BC is medial and is equal to DE, therefore DE is medial. And it is applied to the rational straight line DI, producing DG as breadth; therefore DG is rational and incommensurable in length with DI. [X. 22] Again, since twice the rectangle AB, BC is medial and is equal to DH, therefore DH is medial. And it is applied to the rational straight line DI, producing DF as breadth; therefore DF is also rational and incommensurable in length with DI. [X. 22] And, since the squares on AB, BC are incommensurable with twice the rectangle AB, BC, therefore DE is also incommensurable with DH. But, as DE is to DH, so also is DG to DF; [VI. 1] therefore DG is incommensurable with DF. [X. 11] And both are rational; therefore GD, DF are rational straight lines commensurable in square only. Therefore FG is an apotome. [X. 73] And FH is rational; but the rectangle contained by a rational straight line and an apotome is irrational, [deduction from X. 20] and its “side” is irrational. And AC is the “side” of FE; therefore AC is irrational. And let it be called that which produces with a medial area a medial whole.

10.78
**Statement:** If from a straight line there be subtracted a straight line which is incommensurable in square with the whole and which with the whole makes the sum of the squares on them medial, twice the rectangle contained by them medial, and further the squares on them incommensurable with twice the rectangle contained by them, the remainder is irrational; and let it be called that which produces with a medial area a medial whole.

**Step 1.** Let AB be a straight line and let BC be subtracted from it (C lying on AB), so that AC is the remainder. By hypothesis, AB and BC are incommensurable in square, the sum of the squares on AB, BC is a medial area, twice the rectangle contained by AB, BC is a medial area, and the squares on AB, BC together are incommensurable with twice the rectangle AB, BC. We must show that the remainder AC is irrational.

**Step 2.** Since the straight line AB is cut at C, the squares on AB and BC together are equal to twice the rectangle AB, BC together with the square on AC (2.7). Hence the square on AC is the excess of the squares on AB, BC over twice the rectangle AB, BC (CN3), and twice the rectangle AB, BC, being a part of the squares on AB, BC, is less than them (CN5).

**Step 3.** Let a rational straight line DI be set out (D10.1.3). To DI let there be applied, in a right angle, the rectangle DE equal to the squares on AB, BC, producing DG as breadth (1.44, 1.45); and to DI, on the same side, let there likewise be applied the rectangle DH equal to twice the rectangle AB, BC, producing DF as breadth. Since DH is less than DE (Step 2) and the two rectangles have the same height DI, DF is less than DG; for if DF were not less than DG, DE would be contained in DH, so that DH would be equal to or greater than DE (CN5), which is impossible. Thus F lies between D and G, DH is a part of DE, and the remaining rectangle FE, contained by FG and the height DI, is equal to the excess of DE over DH, that is, to the square on AC (CN3).

**Step 4.** The squares on AB, BC together form a medial area, that is, they are equal to the square on a medial straight line; and DE is equal to them. Therefore DE is the square on a medial straight line, and it is applied to the rational straight line DI, producing DG as breadth. Therefore DG is rational and incommensurable in length with DI (10.22).

**Step 5.** Again, twice the rectangle AB, BC is a medial area, and DH is equal to it; so DH is the square on a medial straight line applied to the rational straight line DI, producing DF as breadth. Therefore DF is also rational and incommensurable in length with DI (10.22).

**Step 6.** Since the squares on AB, BC are incommensurable with twice the rectangle AB, BC, and DE, DH are equal to these respectively, DE is incommensurable with DH. But DE and DH are rectangles under the same height DI; therefore, as DE is to DH, so is DG to DF (6.1). Consequently DG is incommensurable with DF (10.11); that is, DG and DF are incommensurable in length.

**Step 7.** DG is rational and incommensurable in length with DI, so DG is commensurable with DI in square only (D10.1.3), whence the square on DG is commensurable with the square on DI (D10.1.2). In the same way the square on DF is commensurable with the square on DI. Therefore the squares on DG and DF, being commensurable with the same square, are commensurable with one another (10.12), so that DG and DF are commensurable in square (D10.1.2). Combined with Step 6, DG and DF are rational straight lines commensurable in square only.

**Step 8.** Now FG is the remainder when DF is subtracted from DG. From the rational straight line DG there has been subtracted the rational straight line DF which is commensurable with the whole in square only; therefore the remainder FG is irrational, namely an apotome (10.73).

**Step 9.** The rectangle FE is contained by the rational straight line DI (as height) and the irrational straight line FG. I say that FE is irrational. For suppose FE were a rational area (D10.1.4). Then FE would be a rational area applied to the rational straight line DI, producing FG as breadth, and hence FG would be rational and commensurable in length with DI (10.20). But FG is irrational (Step 8), and a straight line cannot be both rational and irrational (D10.1.3). This is impossible; therefore FE is not rational, that is, FE is an irrational area (D10.1.4).

**Step 10.** But FE is equal to the square on AC (Step 3). Therefore the square on AC is an irrational area, and so its side AC, the straight line which produces it, is irrational (D10.1.4). Therefore the remainder AC is irrational, which was to be proved. And since the square on AC, added to the medial area DH (twice the rectangle AB, BC), makes up the medial whole DE (the squares on AB, BC), let AC be called that which produces with a medial area a medial whole.
